paper.title_en: Modelling the Multiplicity Distributions and Modified Combinants in pp Collisions at the LHC Energy
paper.abstract_en: The multiplicity distributions of charged particles and their combinants in pp collisions at LHC energies are studied within the framework of the Multipomeron Exchange Model (MEM) that incorporates string fusion effects. In this paper, we focus on three different approaches to implement a cut-Gaussian distribution for the multiplicity of particles produced from a fixed number of pomerons. These approaches are: (i) a Gaussian distribution with fixed parameters for each number of cut pomerons, (ii) an adjusted Gaussian distribution where parameters are determined by requiring that the mean and scaled variance match those derived from a single string, and (iii) a convolution approach where the distribution for multiple pomerons is built recursively from a cut-Gaussian distribution for a single string. We show that these methods, when combined with the two-particle correlation function of a single string to fix the scaled variance, can reproduce the oscillatory behavior of combinants observed in ALICE and CMS data. The results highlight the sensitivity of combinants to the details of the multiplicity distribution and the importance of properly accounting for particle correlations within the string fragmentation picture.
